# CEO Plan: User Dashboard Page
Generated by /plan-ceo-review (via /autoplan) on 2026-09-10
Branch: main | Mode: SELECTIVE EXPANSION
Repo: gstack-autoplan-chain-zmFsqo (no remote)

## Problem
Members visit three pages after login to resume work, check alerts, and inspect recent
changes. A team walkthrough measured a median of 75s to the next item; the production
number is unknown until the baseline step below runs.

Targets:
- Ship bar (advance the rollout): median login-to-first-completed-task improves at least
  20% vs the control cohort.
- Permanence bar (remove the flag): median at or under 45s absolute, or at least 40% below
  the production baseline if that baseline turns out to be far from 75s, sustained 4 weeks
  at 100%.

Guardrails, measured on the flagged cohort vs control over the same window, evaluated
only once the cumulative flagged sample reaches 1000 sessions (a 2-point rate difference
is noise at 200 sessions):
- completed-task rate within 2 percentage points of control
- permission-error rate within 2 percentage points of control
- dashboard partial-failure rate (any panel failing to load) under 2% of requests

## Vision

### 10x Check
A landing page that already knows the member's next step. Login, and the first thing on
screen is "Resume: <assigned item>" as one dominant button, with alerts and changes below.
No scanning, no decision. Concrete shape: eligibility-ranked actions from the existing
registry, item-level deep links in notifications, activity filtered to "mine". Effort for
that full version: human ~2 weeks / CC ~3 hours. This plan builds the surface that version
needs; multi-action ranking is the separate personalization plan.

## Recommended approach (open taste decision T1)
A) `GET /api/dashboard` aggregate endpoint returning a per-source result envelope
(`{ activity, notifications, quickActions }`, each `{ status, data | error }`, notifications
adding `unreadCount` and a server-issued `snapshot`). Each source returns at most 20
records; the panels link to the existing full pages for more. 200 whenever auth passes;
`?sources=` allowlist for per-panel retry. Alternatives considered: B) three client calls
to existing list endpoints (T1 below; under B the envelope, `?sources=`, and server-issued
snapshot are replaced by per-call responses and the snapshot comes from the notifications
list response); C) post-login smart redirect (deferred as experiment E9).

Mark all as read reuses the existing member-scoped bulk-read API, which already takes a
snapshot time and marks only notifications at or before it. The `snapshot` in the envelope
is the server-issued value the client passes to that existing API. No new mutation API is
introduced anywhere in this plan; E6 is deferred precisely because it would need one.

## Effort for accepted scope
Baseline plan plus E1-E5 and the shared primitives: human ~3 days / CC ~1.5 hours
(the plan file has the hour-by-hour breakdown).

## Scope Decisions

| # | Proposal | Effort | Decision | Reasoning |
|---|----------|--------|----------|-----------|
| E1 | Next-up primary CTA when resume-assigned-work is eligible; when not eligible the three actions render as equal buttons | S | ACCEPTED | Directly moves the metric. Uses only the single existing eligibility predicate for that action; no ordering across actions, so this is not ranking. Ranking stays deferred. |
| E2 | Unread count badge in Notifications header | S | ACCEPTED | Count already needed for Mark-all button state; answers "is there anything?" before scanning |
| E3 | View all links to existing full pages | S | ACCEPTED | Makes the 20-record cap honest; older-page navigation stays where it lives |
| E4 | Relative timestamps with absolute time in title and datetime | S | ACCEPTED | Does not move the 45s metric directly; low cost, faster scanning, screen readers get the absolute value |
| E5 | Refresh when the user returns to the tab, at most every 30s | S | ACCEPTED | Does not move the metric directly; low cost, prevents stale-alert confusion; the 30s floor bounds traffic |
| E6 | Per-notification mark-as-read | M | DEFERRED | Needs a new mutation API, which this plan excludes |
| E7 | Live notification updates | M-L | DEFERRED | Needs polling or push infrastructure this plan does not touch |
| E8 | Keyboard shortcuts for actions | S-M | DEFERRED | Global key handling, screen-reader conflicts; needs its own a11y review |
| E9 | Post-login smart redirect A/B | S | DEFERRED | Login-flow change; needs the production baseline first |

## Accepted Scope (added to this plan)
- E1 Next-up primary CTA
- E2 Unread badge
- E3 View all links
- E4 Relative timestamps
- E5 Refresh on tab return (30s floor)

## Engineering commitments inherited from review (not scope decisions)
These were required by the review to make the baseline scope shippable; they live in
the plan file's Review record with full detail:
- Complete error and rescue map for every panel and for Mark all as read (shape depends on T1)
- Action feedback announced through a screen-reader live region (required by the existing
  accessibility policy regardless of T3; T3 only decides whether the toast component is
  built here or in a separate ticket first)
- Shared panel-state wrapper and a shared server/client contract module
- Production baseline measurement before rollout; the targets and guardrails above; the
  logs, metrics, alerts, and cohort funnel panel that make them observable

## Rollout
1. Baseline: compute median and p75 login-to-first-completed-task over the last 30 days
   from existing analytics events and record it in the plan before any member sees the page.
2. Ramp on `dashboard_landing` (member-cohort flag): staging → internal cohort → 5% → 25% → 100%.
3. Exit criteria for staging and internal cohort: functional only (all three panels load,
   a forced partial failure shows one panel error with a working Retry, mark all as read
   completes, keyboard-only pass, zero accessibility violations).
4. Hold criteria at 5% and 25%: at least 1 week and 200 flagged sessions for the median
   check (ship bar, 20% improvement vs control); guardrails evaluated once the cumulative
   flagged sample reaches 1000 sessions. Roll back one step on a guardrail breach at that
   sample size, or immediately on partial-failure rate over 2%.
5. Permanence: after 4 weeks at 100% with the permanence bar met and guardrails held,
   remove the flag and make the dashboard the landing page. If the permanence bar is not
   met after 8 weeks at 100%, decide explicitly: keep with the ship-bar gain, iterate, or
   roll back.

## Deferred to TODOS.md
- E6 per-notification mark-as-read (P3; depends on a new mutation API)
- E7 live updates (P3; polling or push infrastructure)
- E8 keyboard shortcuts (P3; needs a11y review)
- E9 post-login smart redirect A/B (P2; after baseline and cohort data)
- Remove `dashboard_landing` flag after the permanence bar is met (P2)

## Taste decisions (OPEN — resolved by the user at the /autoplan Final Gate, due before implementation)
Each shows the recommended option first. The plan file proceeds on the recommended option
until the user says otherwise.
- T1 Aggregate endpoint (recommended) vs three client calls. Owner: user at gate.
- T2 All three panels in v1 behind the flag (recommended) vs QuickActions-first staged v1. Owner: user at gate.
- T3 Toast built as shared primitive in this plan (recommended) vs separate ticket first. Owner: user at gate.
- T4 Keep confirmation modal on Mark all as read (recommended; no undo API exists) vs remove modal + undo. Owner: user at gate.
